text:
lina: Heads-up: spike of Pending GPU pods in ap-southeast1 again. ~35 pending, lots of scale-ups that immediately scale down. Cost spike on the billing dashboard.
devon: any scheduler logs?
lina: pasted from scheduler: ```FailedScheduling: 0/48 nodes are available: 38 node(s) didn't match Pod's nodeAffinity; 10 node(s) had taints the pod didn't tolerate; 0/48 nodes have sufficient free gpus```
rajeev: these are short (30s-2m) batch inferencers with label isolation=hard. Folks put that label to guarantee no colocation.
tasha: isolation=hard was added after that noisy-tenant incident in 2023. But now with the regional capacity dip apse1 is tiny and the anti-colocate rule fragments.
lina: autoscaler log shows churn: "scaleUp: 7 nodes added for gpu-pool-apse1 at 02:11, scaleDown: 6 nodes removed at 02:13 (utilization 5%)"
devon: classic coldstart waste. Two possible fixes: use a tiny warm pool (min 2 nodes) for these namespaces OR change to preferred anti-affinity.
rajeev: another option: enable MIG partitions for those workloads so multiple inferencers can share a single physical GPU. That would preserve isolation but improve packability.
tasha: do we have MIG-capable instances in ap-southeast1?
devon: yes we launched a small MIG fleet last quarter for model tuning. It's labelled node.k8s.io/gpu-mig=true.
lina: would need admission mutation to prefer MIG nodes for pods with resource.gpu_mig_request=small. Can do via a mutating webhook.
rajeev: if we go MIG route we must ensure the container runtime requests the right device plugin and limit the memory slice. Also check model perf under MIG slices.
tasha: short-term: I'd like a low-friction mitigation to stop autoscaler flipping. Proposal: 1) mutate pods in the public-infer ns to change hard anti-affinity to preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution (weight: 70) and 2) add a 15m scale-down-delay for gpu-pool-apse1.
devon: sounds reasonable. Also add a scheduler policy tweak: prefer nodes with existing same-label pods (score boost) so scheduler fills before launching new nodes.
lina: risk callout: some teams relied on strict isolation for privacy. We must scope mutation to namespace public-infer and only for pods with label isolation=hard & annotation allow-relax=true. Otherwise no mutation.
rajeev: can we instead use a nodeSelector to route to MIG nodes for small jobs? That avoids changing affinity. We can convert small jobs automatically to set nodeSelector: node.k8s.io/gpu-mig=true and resource.gpu_mig_request=1/4 via webhook.
tasha: let's not rewrite resource quantities - that could break metrics. Prefer adding preferredAffinity or nodeSelector only.
devon: monitoring: create dashboard panels for Pending GPU pods, Node provisioning events, and per-node GPU util. Add alert: Pending GPU pods > 20 for 5m.
lina: I'll prototype a mutating webhook that: if namespace==public-infer && labels.isolation==hard && annotation.allow-relax=="true" then add preferred anti-affinity weight:70 and add nodeSelector to prefer node.k8s.io/gpu-mig=true if pod annotation request-mig=="true".
rajeev: I'll validate MIG perf on a small perf run (50 pods) in staging against the MIG fleet. If perf degrades we abort.
tasha: ops-bot: please schedule a 1-hour canary window for ap-southeast1 after the maintenance window so we can test the webhook.
ops-bot: NOTE: maintenance window 04:00-05:00 UTC. Canary window for ap-southeast1 allowed 06:00-07:00 UTC.
lina: action items:
- lina -> implement mutating webhook draft and unit tests
- devon -> scheduler scoring PR to prefer filling GPU nodes
- rajeev -> run MIG perf validation on staging
- tasha -> set autoscaler scale-down-delay=15m for gpu-pool-apse1 and create Pending-pods alert

rajeev: timeline: aim canary tomorrow 06:00 UTC. I'll own rollback if MIG perf bad.
devon: also notify cost team and mark node annotations so we can attribute reserved warm nodes.
ops-bot: REMINDER: avoid disruptive cluster changes during maintenance window.
lina: ok will land webhook after canary pass. posting updates here. :shipit:
